title: Inventory management with stock control and reporting
prompt:
Build an inventory management system in Python.

Modules:
- product.py: `class Product(sku: str, name: str, price: float, quantity: int = 0)` with those attributes. Raises `ValueError` if price < 0 or quantity < 0.
- inventory.py: `class Inventory`.
  - `add_product(product)` raises `ValueError` if a product with the same sku already exists.
  - `get(sku)` returns the Product; raises `KeyError` for an unknown sku.
  - `restock(sku, qty)` increases the quantity; raises `ValueError` if qty <= 0 and `KeyError` for an unknown sku.
  - `sell(sku, qty)` decreases the quantity and returns the sale amount (price * qty); raises `ValueError` if qty <= 0 or qty is more than the quantity in stock (stock unchanged in that case).
  - `total_value()` returns the sum of price * quantity over all products.
  - `low_stock(threshold=5)` returns a sorted list of the skus whose quantity is below the threshold.
- report.py: `format_report(inventory) -> str`. One line per product, sorted by sku, formatted `<sku> | <name> | <quantity> | <price with 2 decimals>`, followed by a final line `TOTAL: <total value with 2 decimals>`.
- main.py: command-line interface. Read commands from standard input, one per line, until `quit` or end of input:
  - `add <sku> <price> <quantity> <name words...>`
  - `sell <sku> <qty>` prints `Sold: <amount with 2 decimals>`
  - `restock <sku> <qty>`
  - `report` prints the output of format_report
  - On any error print a line starting with `Error:` and continue.

Constraints: use only the Python standard library. The entry point is main.py in the project root, guarded by `if __name__ == "__main__":`.
smoke_stdin:
add A1 2.50 10 blue pen
report
quit
